objects.definition: typedef uint8_t yyjson_type;
objects.description: 3-bit type tag used internally and by API to represent the JSON value type (raw, null, bool, num, str, arr, obj).

objects.definition: typedef uint8_t yyjson_subtype;
objects.description: 2-bit subtype tag for JSON values (e.g., bool true/false, number kind, string escaping subtype).
Pluggable memory allocator used by yyjson readers/writers and mutable docs. Provide malloc/realloc/free with an optional user context.

objects.definition: typedef struct yyjson_doc yyjson_doc;
objects.description: Opaque immutable JSON document handle that owns all yyjson_val nodes and strings. Free with yyjson_doc_free().

objects.definition: typedef struct yyjson_val yyjson_val;
objects.description: Opaque immutable JSON value node belonging to a yyjson_doc. Lifetime tied to its document; cannot be freed individually.

objects.definition: typedef struct yyjson_mut_doc yyjson_mut_doc;
objects.description: Opaque mutable JSON document for building/editing JSON. Manages pools for values and strings. Free with yyjson_mut_doc_free().

objects.definition: typedef struct yyjson_mut_val yyjson_mut_val;
objects.description: Opaque mutable JSON value node allocated from a yyjson_mut_doc. Used to construct and modify JSON trees.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t yyjson_read_flag;
objects.description: Bitmask of run-time options for the JSON reader (e.g., in-situ, comments, JSON5, etc.).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t yyjson_read_code;
objects.description: Result code enumeration for the JSON reader indicating success or a specific error condition.
Error info for reader: code, message (static), and byte position.

objects.definition: typedef struct yyjson_incr_state yyjson_incr_state;
objects.description: Opaque state object for incremental JSON reading; create with yyjson_incr_new() and free with yyjson_incr_free().

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t yyjson_write_flag;
objects.description: Bitmask of run-time options for the JSON writer (pretty, escaping, FP formatting, etc.).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t yyjson_write_code;
objects.description: Result code enumeration for the JSON writer indicating success or the type of write error.
Error info for writer: code and static message string.
Iterator state for traversing immutable arrays. Not heap-allocated; no destructor needed.
Iterator state for traversing immutable objects. Not heap-allocated; no destructor needed.
Iterator state for traversing mutable arrays with support for removing current element. Not heap-allocated.
Iterator state for traversing mutable objects with ability to remove current pair. Not heap-allocated.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t yyjson_ptr_code;
objects.description: Result code enumeration for JSON Pointer operations.
Error info for JSON Pointer parsing/resolution: code, message, and byte position in pointer string.
Context capturing container and sibling info for subsequent pointer-based append/replace/remove without re-parsing.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t yyjson_patch_code;
objects.description: Result code enumeration for JSON Patch (RFC 6902) operations.
Error info for JSON Patch operations including failing operation index and nested pointer error.
Internal payload union for value storage: numbers, string pointer, container pointer/offset. For implementation use.
Concrete definition of immutable value: 16 bytes, tag encodes type/subtype/length; uni holds payload.
Concrete immutable document structure: root value, allocator copy, read stats, and owned string pool pointer.
Concrete mutable value: tag/payload plus next pointer to form circular linked lists for containers.
Internal string pool chunk header for mutable docs; forms a linked list of string memory blocks.
Internal string memory pool for yyjson_mut_doc to allocate and own copied strings efficiently.
Internal value pool chunk header for allocating batches of yyjson_mut_val nodes.
Internal pool allocator for mutable value nodes managed by yyjson_mut_doc.
Concrete mutable document structure owning root, allocator, and internal pools for strings and values.

functions.name: yyjson_version
functions.description: Returns the yyjson library version encoded as (major<<16)|(minor<<8)|(patch). Use to check runtime library version against compile-time macros.
requirements: None beyond normal function call semantics.

functions.name: yyjson_alc_pool_init
functions.signature: yyjson_api bool yyjson_alc_pool_init(yyjson_alc *alc, void *buf, size_t size);
functions.description: Initializes a pool allocator that uses a caller-provided fixed buffer to avoid malloc/realloc during parsing/writing. Intended for a single JSON document at a time.
requirements: alc must not be NULL.
buf must not be NULL.
size must be at least 8 words (32/64 bytes on 32/64-bit OS).
Not thread-safe.

functions.name: yyjson_alc_dyn_new
functions.description: Creates a dynamic allocator that grows using malloc internally and can free all allocations at once when destroyed.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Not thread-safe.

functions.name: yyjson_alc_dyn_free
functions.description: Frees a dynamic allocator previously created by yyjson_alc_dyn_new().
requirements: alc should be a dynamic allocator returned by yyjson_alc_dyn_new().
Safe to pass NULL (function does nothing).

functions.name: yyjson_locate_pos
functions.signature: yyjson_api bool yyjson_locate_pos(const char *str, size_t len, size_t pos, size_t *line, size_t *col, size_t *chr);
functions.description: Computes 1-based line and column, and 0-based character index for a byte position in a UTF-8 string, useful for error reporting.
requirements: str must not be NULL.
pos must be within [0,len].
line/col/chr may be NULL if caller does not need those outputs.

functions.name: yyjson_read_opts
functions.signature: yyjson_api yyjson_doc *yyjson_read_opts(char *dat, size_t len, yyjson_read_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc, yyjson_read_err *err);
functions.description: Parses JSON from a buffer with options and optional custom allocator and error reporting. May modify input when YYJSON_READ_INSITU is used.
requirements: dat must not be NULL.
len must be > 0.
If YYJSON_READ_INSITU flag is set, dat must be writable and padded by at least YYJSON_PADDING_SIZE bytes, and caller must retain the data while the document lives.
alc may be NULL to use default allocator.
err may be NULL if error info not needed.
Thread-safe if dat is not modified concurrently and alc is thread-safe or NULL.
On success, free result with yyjson_doc_free().

functions.name: yyjson_read_file
functions.signature: yyjson_api yyjson_doc *yyjson_read_file(const char *path, yyjson_read_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc, yyjson_read_err *err);
functions.description: Parses JSON from a file path with options and optional allocator and error reporting.
requirements: path must be a valid null-terminated path string; must not be NULL.
alc may be NULL to use default allocator.
err may be NULL if error info not needed.
Thread-safe if file is not concurrently modified and alc is thread-safe or NULL.
On 32-bit OS, files >2GB may fail.
On success, free result with yyjson_doc_free().

functions.name: yyjson_read_fp
functions.signature: yyjson_api yyjson_doc *yyjson_read_fp(FILE *fp, yyjson_read_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc, yyjson_read_err *err);
functions.description: Parses JSON from the current position of a FILE* to EOF with options.
requirements: fp must not be NULL and must be valid for reading.
alc may be NULL to use default allocator.
err may be NULL if error info not needed.
Thread-safe if file is not concurrently accessed and alc is thread-safe or NULL.
On 32-bit OS, files >2GB may fail.
On success, free result with yyjson_doc_free().

functions.name: yyjson_read
functions.signature: yyjson_api_inline yyjson_doc *yyjson_read(const char *dat, size_t len, yyjson_read_flag flg);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for yyjson_read_opts() that ensures in-situ is disabled for const input and uses default allocator and no error reporting.
requirements: dat must not be NULL.
len must be > 0.
Returns document to be freed with yyjson_doc_free().

functions.name: yyjson_incr_new
functions.signature: yyjson_api yyjson_incr_state *yyjson_incr_new(char *buf, size_t buf_len, yyjson_read_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc);
functions.description: Creates an incremental JSON reader state to parse a large JSON in chunks. Non-standard flags are ignored; only standard JSON is supported.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
buf_len is the current available bytes; if YYJSON_READ_INSITU is used, buf_len must exclude padding.
alc may be NULL to use default allocator.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Free with yyjson_incr_free().

functions.name: yyjson_incr_read
functions.description: Feeds up to len more bytes into the incremental reader. Returns a document when complete. If returns NULL with err->code==YYJSON_READ_ERROR_MORE, provide more data and call again.
requirements: state must be created by yyjson_incr_new() and not NULL.
len must be > 0.
err may be NULL if error info not needed.
On success, caller must free returned document with yyjson_doc_free().
Small increments are inefficient; prefer KB/MB increments.

functions.name: yyjson_incr_free
functions.description: Frees an incremental reader state created by yyjson_incr_new().
requirements: state may be NULL (no effect).

functions.name: yyjson_read_max_memory_usage
functions.signature: yyjson_api_inline size_t yyjson_read_max_memory_usage(size_t len, yyjson_read_flag flg);
functions.description: Calculates an upper bound on memory needed to parse a JSON of given length with flags, useful for sizing a pool allocator.
requirements: len is the input length in bytes; if YYJSON_READ_STOP_WHEN_DONE is set and len<256, it is rounded up internally.
Returns 0 on overflow.

functions.name: yyjson_read_number
functions.signature: yyjson_api const char *yyjson_read_number(const char *dat, yyjson_val *val, yyjson_read_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc, yyjson_read_err *err);
functions.description: Parses a single JSON number from a null-terminated string, writing the result into a yyjson_val (number or raw depending on flags). Returns pointer to char after last consumed character on success.
requirements: dat must not be NULL and must be null-terminated.
val must not be NULL.
Supports YYJSON_READ_NUMBER_AS_RAW and YYJSON_READ_ALLOW_INF_AND_NAN flags; other flags are ignored.
alc is used only when fast FP conversion is disabled; may be NULL to use default.
err may be NULL.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: yyjson_mut_read_number
functions.signature: yyjson_api_inline const char *yyjson_mut_read_number(const char *dat, yyjson_mut_val *val, yyjson_read_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc, yyjson_read_err *err);
functions.description: Same as yyjson_read_number() but writes into a mutable value.
requirements: Same requirements as yyjson_read_number().

functions.name: yyjson_write_opts
functions.signature: yyjson_api char *yyjson_write_opts(const yyjson_doc *doc, yyjson_write_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc, size_t *len, yyjson_write_err *err);
functions.description: Serializes an immutable document to a newly allocated UTF-8 string with options. Optionally returns length and error info.
requirements: doc must not be NULL and must have a root.
flg may combine write flags.
alc may be NULL to use default allocator.
len and err may be NULL if not needed.
On success, returned string must be freed with free() or alc->free().
Thread-safe if alc is thread-safe or NULL.

functions.name: yyjson_write_file
functions.signature: yyjson_api bool yyjson_write_file(const char *path, const yyjson_doc *doc, yyjson_write_flag flg, const yyjson_alc *alc, yyjson_write_err *err);
functions.description: Writes an immutable document to a file at path with options.
requirements: path must be a valid null-terminated path; must not be NULL.
doc must not be NULL and must have a root.

functions.name: yyjson_write_buf
functions.signature: yyjson_api size_t yyjson_write_buf(char *buf, size_t buf_len, const yyjson_doc *doc, yyjson_write_flag flg, yyjson_write_err *err);
functions.description: Serializes an immutable document into a caller-provided buffer without allocations. Returns bytes written (excluding null terminator) or 0 on failure. Buffer must be larger than final size to permit temporary space.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
buf_len must be large enough or function returns 0.
doc must not be NULL and must have a root.
err may be NULL if not needed.
See API.md for buffer sizing details.

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for UTF-8 text buffers suited for yyjson string-accepting APIs.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid UTF-8
# - Include variety: ASCII, multibyte, control chars, newlines, long/short, edge cases
# - Sometimes include JSON pointer-friendly characters (/ ~ 0 1), object key-like tokens, numbers
# - Limit to <= 4096 bytes
# - Random but seeded

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "kappa", "omega", "node", "value",
    "key", "name", "id", "title", "description", "path", "user", "email",
    "true", "false", "null", "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity",
]

JSONISH_SNIPPETS = [
    "key", "value", "foo", "bar", "baz", "qux", "data", "items", "list",
    "0", "1", "2", "10", "-1", "18446744073709551615", "-9223372036854775808",
    "3.14159", "2.9979e8", "-0.0",
]

# A set of valid Unicode scalars to compose multibyte UTF-8 strings
UNICODE_CODEPOINT_BUCKETS = [
    # ASCII range (1-byte)
    list(range(0x20, 0x7F)),
    # Common Latin-1 supplement
    [0x00A0, 0x00A9, 0x00AE, 0x00B5, 0x00D7, 0x00F7, 0x00FF],
    # Latin Extended, Greek, Cyrillic
    [0x0101, 0x017F, 0x0391, 0x03C9, 0x0401, 0x044F],
    # Emoji and symbols
    [0x1F600, 0x1F602, 0x1F609, 0x1F60D, 0x1F622, 0x1F680, 0x1F4A9],
    # CJK range samples
    [0x4E2D, 0x6587, 0x65E5, 0x672C, 0x8A9E],
]

# Characters useful for JSON Pointer exercises
POINTER_CHARS = "/~01"  # '/', '~', '0', '1'

def _rand_cp(r: random.Random) -> int:
    bucket = r.choice(UNICODE_CODEPOINT_BUCKETS)
    cp = r.choice(bucket)
    return cp

def _encode_utf8_codepoint(cp: int) -> bytes:
    return chr(cp).encode('utf-8')

def _make_multibyte_chunk(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(1, max(1, min(16, max_len)))
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        out += _encode_utf8_codepoint(_rand_cp(r))
    return bytes(out)

def _make_ascii_chunk(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Include letters, digits, underscore, dash, spaces, punctuation.
    alphabet = (
        "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
        "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
        "0123456789"
        "_- .,:;!@#$%^&*()[]{}<>?"  # include punctuation
    )
    n = r.randint(1, max(1, min(32, max_len)))
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-8')

def _make_newline_chunk(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of newlines and tabs to exercise locate_pos line/col/chr
    choices = ['\n', '\r', '\t']
    n = r.randint(1, max(1, min(64, max_len)))
    return ''.join(r.choice(choices) for _ in range(n)).encode('utf-8')

def _make_pointer_like(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build something like a JSON Pointer path without leading slash (caller may prepend)
    # Include escaped sequences like ~0 and ~1, segments, digits
    seg_cnt = r.randint(1, 6)
    segs = []
    for _ in range(seg_cnt):
        seg_len = r.randint(0, max(0, min(12, max_len)))
        seg = []
        for _j in range(seg_len):
            # Occasionally insert escape sequence
            if r.random() < 0.15:
                seg.append(r.choice(["~0", "~1"]))
            else:
                ch = r.choice(ASCII_WORDS + JSONISH_SNIPPETS)
                seg.append(ch)
        segs.append(''.join(seg))
    path = '/'.join(segs)
    return path.encode('utf-8')

def _make_key_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Keys suitable for object operations; include variety and multibyte occasionally
    base = r.choice(ASCII_WORDS + JSONISH_SNIPPETS)
    tail = ''
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        tail = '_' + str(r.randint(0, 9999))
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        # add multibyte flair
        tail += chr(_rand_cp(r))
    return (base + tail).encode('utf-8')

def _make_value_like(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Values for str/raw; mix ascii words, numbers, multibyte, and whitespace
    parts = []
    budget = max_len
    while budget > 0 and len(parts) < 8:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.35:
            chunk = _make_ascii_chunk(r, min(32, budget))
        elif choice < 0.65:
            chunk = _make_multibyte_chunk(r, min(24, budget))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            chunk = _make_newline_chunk(r, min(16, budget))
        else:
            chunk = r.choice([b"true", b"false", b"null", b"0", b"1", b"-1", b"3.14", b"2.71828"]) 
        if not chunk:
            break
        parts.append(chunk)
        budget -= len(chunk)
        if budget > 0 and r.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(b" ")
            budget -= 1
    return b''.join(parts)[:max_len]

def _maybe_null_terminated(buf: bytes, r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Many APIs accept non-NUL-terminated with explicit length; some require NUL.
    # We will sometimes append a trailing NUL to cover both.
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return buf
    # Ensure single trailing NUL but keep overall size limit consideration to caller
    return buf + b"\x00"

def _compose_interesting_utf8(r: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose a buffer from a palette of chunk generators to cover many API uses
    parts = []
    remaining = budget

    # Sometimes generate a pointer-like path starting with '/'
    if r.random() < 0.4 and remaining > 0:
        frag = _make_pointer_like(r, min(64, remaining))
        p = b"/" + frag
        p = p[:remaining]
        parts.append(p)
        remaining -= len(p)
        # maybe newline after pointer to exercise locate_pos
        if remaining > 0 and r.random() < 0.5:
            nl = _make_newline_chunk(r, min(8, remaining))
            parts.append(nl)
            remaining -= len(nl)

    # Add several key-like/value-like chunks
    while remaining > 0 and len(parts) < 12:
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.25:
            chunk = _make_key_like(r)
        elif t < 0.55:
            chunk = _make_value_like(r, min(64, remaining))
        elif t < 0.75:
            chunk = _make_multibyte_chunk(r, min(48, remaining))
        else:
            chunk = _make_ascii_chunk(r, min(64, remaining))
        if not chunk:
            break
        chunk = chunk[:remaining]
        parts.append(chunk)
        remaining -= len(chunk)
        if remaining > 0 and r.random() < 0.5:
            sep = r.choice([b"\n", b"\t", b" ", b"/", b"::", b",", b"|"])
            sep = sep[:remaining]
            parts.append(sep)
            remaining -= len(sep)

    data = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure valid UTF-8 by construction; trim to budget
    return data[:budget]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide a target size within limits; prefer small to moderate but allow larger
    size = r.choice([
        r.randint(0, 32),
        r.randint(33, 128),
        r.randint(129, 512),
        r.randint(513, 2048),
    ])
    size = min(size, 4096)

    buf = _compose_interesting_utf8(r, size)

    # Occasionally force special small or edge cases regardless of composed size
    special = r.random()
    if special < 0.08:
        buf = b""  # empty buffer (valid for many n-length APIs and empty pointer cases)
    elif special < 0.15:
        # Only newlines to stress line/col in locate_pos
        n = r.randint(1, 256)
        buf = ("\n\r\t" * ((n + 2)//3))[:n].encode('utf-8')
    elif special < 0.22:
        # Deep pointer-like path
        segs = [r.choice(ASCII_WORDS) for _ in range(r.randint(5, 20))]
        buf = ("/" + "/".join(segs)).encode('utf-8')
    elif special < 0.28:
        # Many multibyte characters
        parts = [_make_multibyte_chunk(r, 8) for _ in range(r.randint(8, 64))]
        buf = b''.join(parts)[:size]

    # Optionally append NUL terminator to satisfy no-copy C-string APIs
    buf = _maybe_null_terminated(buf, r)

    # Ensure we don't exceed maximum allowed output
    return buf[:4096]

import random

# Generator for interesting arbitrary byte buffers used as string/raw inputs for yyjson APIs.
# The buffers are used along with explicit lengths, so embedded NULs are allowed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

_JSON_SNIPPETS = [
    b"",  # empty buffer (length 0)
    b"null",
    b"true",
    b"false",
    b"0",
    b"-0",
    b"1",
    b"-1",
    b"1234567890",
    b"1.0",
    b"-1.25",
    b"1e10",
    b"-2E-5",
    b"\"\"",
    b"\"a\"",
    b"\"\\\\\"/\\b\\f\\n\\r\\t\"",  # string with escapes
    b"[]",
    b"[1,2,3]",
    b"[true,false,null]",
    b"{}",
    b"{\"a\":1}",
    b"{\"a\":\"b\"}",
    b"{\"nested\":{\"k\":[1,2,{\"x\":\"y\"}]}}",
]

# Keys to exercise object lookups/renames/removals, including empty and special chars.
_KEY_CASES = [
    b"",
    b"a",
    b"A",
    b"0",
    b"_",
    b"-",
    b"key",
    b"Key",
    b"k e y",     # contains space
    b"k\t\tey",  # contains tabs
    b"k\nkey",    # newline
    b"k\x00ey",  # embedded NUL
    b"k\"ey",    # quote
    b"slash/seg", # contains slash
    b"~tilde~",   # tilde for JSON Pointer style
    b"unicode-\xe2\x9c\x93",  # '✓' in UTF-8
]

# Raw binary payloads to stress non-text handling
_RAW_PAYLOADS = [
    bytes(range(256)),                 # 0..255
    b"\x00\x00\x00",
    b"\xff\x00\xff\x00",
    b"\x7f\x80\x81\xfe\xff",
    b"bin\x00ary\x01\x02data",
]


def _repeat_chunk(chunk: bytes, n: int, limit: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    out = chunk * n
    return out[:limit]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _utf8_sequences() -> list[bytes]:
    # All encoded with escape sequences to avoid non-ASCII bytes in literals
    return [
        b"ascii",
        b"\xcf\x80",                   # 'π'
        b"\xe4\xb8\xad\xe6\x96\x87", # '中文'
        b"\xf0\x9f\x98\x80",         # '😀'
        b"e\xcc\x81",                  # 'e' + combining acute
        b"\xf0\x9d\x94\x98\xf0\x9d\x94\xab\xf0\x9d\x94\xa6\xf0\x9d\x94\xa0\xf0\x9d\x94\xb8\xf0\x9d\x94\xa2\xf0\x9d\x94\xa6",  # Fraktur 'Unicode'
    ]


def _make_pool(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    pool: list[bytes] = []
    pool.extend(_JSON_SNIPPETS)
    pool.extend(_KEY_CASES)
    pool.extend(_RAW_PAYLOADS)
    pool.extend(_utf8_sequences())

    # JSON-like big arrays/objects to drive iter/lookup paths
    pool.append(_repeat_chunk(b"a", 256, 256))
    pool.append(_repeat_chunk(b"k", 1024, 1024))

    # Mixed content with NULs and UTF-8
    pool.append(b"pre\x00mid\x00post")
    pool.append(b"\x00")  # UTF-8 NUL

    # Construct a compact JSON object with many keys to help find and rename
    keys = [b"a", b"b", b"c", b"d", b"e", b"f", b"g"]
    obj_parts = []
    for i, k in enumerate(keys):
        obj_parts.append(b'"' + k.replace(b'"', b'\\"') + b'":' + str(i).encode())
    pool.append(b"{" + b",".join(obj_parts) + b"}")

    # JSON arrays of strings (used by arr_with_strn/strncpy)
    arr_strs = [b'"'+s.replace(b'"', b'\\"')+b'"' for s in [b"a", b"", b"nul\x00", b"\xe2\x9c\x93"]]
    pool.append(b"[" + b",".join(arr_strs) + b"]")

    # Edge: long but valid UTF-8 (Cyrillic "абвгд" repeated)
    long_utf8 = (b"\xd0\xb0\xd0\xb1\xd0\xb2\xd0\xb3\xd0\xb4" * 200)
    pool.append(long_utf8[:1500])

    # Edge: random but limited length blobs
    for n in [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256]:
        pool.append(_rand_bytes(rng, n))

    return [p for p in pool if len(p) <= MAX_SIZE]


def _maybe_embed(rng: random.Random, base: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes wrap base in JSON constructs or append/prepend bytes to vary positions
    choice = rng.randrange(6)
    if choice == 0:
        return base
    if choice == 1:
        return b'"' + base.replace(b'"', b'\\"') + b'"'  # quoted JSON string
    if choice == 2:
        return b"[" + base + b"]"
    if choice == 3:
        return b"{" + b'"k"' + b":" + base + b"}"
    if choice == 4:
        pad_left = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 8))
        pad_right = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 8))
        return pad_left + base + pad_right
    # choice == 5
    if len(base) < MAX_SIZE - 16:
        return base + b"\x00" + _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 8))
    return base


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pool = _make_pool(rng)

    # Choose a strategy corresponding to different stub usage contexts:
    #  - object keys (short, varied)
    #  - string values (UTF-8, may contain NULs)
    #  - raw blobs
    #  - JSON snippets for raw/string set
    strategy = rng.randrange(6)

    if strategy == 0:
        # Likely object key usage: short string with special chars
        candidate = rng.choice(_KEY_CASES)
        # Occasionally duplicate to be longer
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            repeat = rng.randint(1, 16)
            candidate = (candidate * repeat)[:512]
        return candidate

    if strategy == 1:
        # UTF-8 text values
        candidate = rng.choice(_utf8_sequences())
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # concatenate multiple utf8 sequences
            parts = [rng.choice(_utf8_sequences()) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8))]
            candidate = b"".join(parts)
        # maybe interleave NULs which are valid with explicit length
        if rng.random() < 0.4 and len(candidate) < 1024:
            inter = []
            for bch in candidate:
                inter.append(bytes([bch]))
                if rng.random() < 0.2:
                    inter.append(b"\x00")
            candidate = b"".join(inter)
        return candidate[:MAX_SIZE]

    if strategy == 2:
        # Raw binary payloads
        base = rng.choice(_RAW_PAYLOADS)
        # sometimes extend with random bytes
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            base += _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
        return base[:MAX_SIZE]

    if strategy == 3:
        # JSON snippet as content (useful for set_raw to later parse elsewhere)
        base = rng.choice(_JSON_SNIPPETS)
        return base

    if strategy == 4:
        # Array of strings scenario: build comma-joined values or repeated patterns
        count = rng.randint(0, 6)
        vals = []
        for _ in range(count):
            # choose among utf8/key/raw small pieces
            pick = rng.choice([rng.choice(_utf8_sequences()), rng.choice(_KEY_CASES), _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 8))])
            vals.append(pick)
        # produce one value; fuzzer harness will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times
        data = b"".join(vals)
        return data[:MAX_SIZE]

    # strategy == 5
    # Start from pool and maybe embed/wrap/pad
    base = rng.choice(pool)
    data = _maybe_embed(rng, base)
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid JSON Pointer strings to exercise yyjson pointer APIs.
# We aim to cover:
# - empty pointer ""
# - object-like keys with special chars (including '/' and '~' via escapes)
# - array indices: 0, small/large numbers, leading zeros, "-" (append position in patch semantics, though yyjson may treat as key)
# - mixed depth, varying number of tokens
# - tokens that look like integers but exceed 64-bit or have leading +/spaces (as plain strings)
# - Unicode in UTF-8
# The fuzzer stubs prepend '/' themselves in many cases, but some accept empty pointers too.
# We therefore return either "" or a pointer that already begins with '/'.

MAX_LEN = 4096

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "спутник",           # Cyrillic
    "こんにちは",        # Japanese
    "🙂",                # Emoji
    "καλημέρα",         # Greek
    "Résumé",            # Latin with accents
    "δοκιμή",            # Greek
    "מבחן",              # Hebrew
    "اختبار",            # Arabic
]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-."

def esc_token(raw: str) -> str:
    # RFC 6901 escaping for token content: '~' -> '~0', '/' -> '~1'
    return raw.replace('~', '~0').replace('/', '~1')

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

def int_like_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    nums = [
        "0", "1", "2", "10", "99", "100", "1234567890",
        "000", "001", "00010",  # leading zeros
        str(2**31-1), str(2**31), str(2**63-1), str(2**63),
        str(10**19),  # very large
    ]
    # Some strings that look numeric but are not valid indices (still valid tokens)
    nums += ["-", "+1", " 1", "01 ", "1 ", "\t2", "3\n"]
    return nums

def special_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Include characters that must be escaped inside tokens
    specials = [
        esc_token("a/b"),
        esc_token("a~b"),
        esc_token("/~"),
        esc_token("~~"),
        esc_token("/"),
        esc_token("~"),
        esc_token("/~/a~b/c"),
    ]
    # Add some unicode tokens (they'll be escaped only for '/' and '~')
    for u in UNICODE_SAMPLES:
        specials.append(esc_token(u))
    return specials

def build_token_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool = []
    pool += [esc_token(rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8)) for _ in range(8)]
    pool += int_like_tokens(rng)
    pool += special_tokens(rng)
    # Edge: empty token is not possible between separators per RFC, but a trailing
    # or duplicate '/' could be produced by stubs. We will avoid generating empty tokens here.
    return pool

def make_pointer_from_tokens(tokens: List[str]) -> str:
    return "/" + "/".join(tokens) if tokens else ""

def gen_pointer(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide empty vs non-empty pointer
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        return ""  # empty pointer

    pool = build_token_pool(rng)

    # Depth selection: prefer a range 1..6, sometimes deeper
    depth = rng.choices([1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10], weights=[20,20,16,12,10,8,2,2], k=1)[0]

    tokens = []
    for i in range(depth):
        choice = rng.choice(pool)
        # Occasionally make a long token
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            long_part = esc_token(rand_ascii(rng, 16, 64))
            choice = choice + long_part if rng.random() < 0.5 else long_part + choice
        tokens.append(choice)

    # Occasionally create an array-heavy tail like /0/1/2
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        tail_len = rng.randint(1, 5)
        tokens += [str(rng.randint(0, 20)) for _ in range(tail_len)]

    # Occasionally insert a token that is exactly "-" (commonly used by RFC6902); still valid token text
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        insert_pos = rng.randrange(0, len(tokens)+1)
        tokens.insert(insert_pos, "-")

    ptr = make_pointer_from_tokens(tokens)
    # Ensure length limit
    if len(ptr.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_LEN:
        # Trim by reducing tokens
        while tokens and len(make_pointer_from_tokens(tokens).encode('utf-8')) > MAX_LEN:
            tokens.pop()
        ptr = make_pointer_from_tokens(tokens)
        if len(ptr.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_LEN:
            ptr = ""  # fallback to empty within budget
    return ptr


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Mix deterministic and random elements per call while being seeded
    # Generate a pointer string according to above strategy
    ptr = gen_pointer(rng)

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes; stubs expect C-string semantics and may prepend '/'
    data = ptr.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > MAX_LEN:
        data = data[:MAX_LEN]
    return data
